tool.name: chainStitchId
tool.description: join chain fragments that share a chain ID
tool.command: chainStitchId '$input' '$output' && ## chainStitchId does not check its writes: the output must have one chain per input chain ID and end with a newline ids_in=\$(awk '$1 == "chain" {print $13}' '$input' | sort -u | wc -l) && chains_out=\$(awk '$1 == "chain"' '$output' | wc -l) && if [ "\$chains_out" -ne "\$ids_in" ] || [ -n "\$(tail -c 1 '$output')" ]; then echo 'The output is incomplete, for example because the disk is full' >&2 && exit 1; fi
tool.help:
**What it does**
`chainStitchId`_ joins the fragments of a pairwise alignment `chain`_ back into whole chains. It finds the fragments by their shared chain ID. It adds the scores of the fragments together and sorts the result by score.
**Why fragments occur**
``netChainSubset`` keeps only the parts of each chain that a net uses. When a net uses one chain in several places, ``netChainSubset`` writes that chain as several fragments with the same ID. UCSC's pairwise alignment pipeline uses this tool to join the fragments again. It does this before it makes the liftOver chain (``doBlastzChainNet.pl``), and before each ``chainSwap`` in the reciprocal-best step (``doRecipBest.pl``).
**Input**
A chain file. The fragments of one chain must come from the same original chain, and they must not overlap. If fragments with the same ID have a different target, query or query strand, the tool stops with an error. If no chain needs joining, the tool sorts the chains by score and removes the ``#`` comment lines. An empty file gives an empty output.
**Output**
A chain file with one chain per ID, sorted by score.
For implementation details see chainStitchId's `source code`_.
.. _chainStitchId: http://hgdownload.cse.ucsc.edu/admin/exe/linux.x86_64/FOOTER.txt .. _chain: https://genome.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/help/chain.html .. _source code: https://github.com/ucscGenomeBrowser/kent/blob/master/src/hg/mouseStuff/chainStitchId/chainStitchId.c
